title: Grateful Dead Live at Denver Coliseum on 1973-11-21
lineage: CD -> Cool Edit Pro v2.0 -> Samplitude Professional v9.12 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: Pristine Miller soundboard capture of a high‑energy late‑’73 show, highlighted by a smoking Mississippi Half‑Step → Playing in the Band → El Paso → Wharf Rat → Morning Dew suite and stellar Here Comes Sunshine.
ai_review.review: The Miller SBD fix delivers crystal‑clear sound with expertly spliced audience patches, making the recording virtually flawless aside from minor labeling quirks. Musically the concert is a late‑1973 powerhouse: the first set shines on Jack Straw and Here Comes Sunshine, while the second set dazzles with an extraordinary Half‑Step/Playing in the Band/El Paso/Wharf Rat/Morning Dew sequence and a knockout One More Saturday Night. Overall energy is high and the band’s interplay—especially Jerry’s soaring solos, Phil’s weaving bass lines, and Keith’s rhythmic wizardry—is consistently praised.

ai_rating.rationale: Average rating ~4.5 from 19 reviews, with overwhelming praise for both performance and soundboard transfer; only a few low‑star outliers do not affect the overall high assessment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean Miller SBD fix with well‑spliced audience patches; minor complaints about lack of track/label info but no audible dropouts or distortion.

standout_songs: Playing in the Band > El Paso > Wharf Rat > Morning Dew
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set flows smoothly with strong vocal harmonies; second set is a masterclass in late‑'73 jazz‑rock continuity, linking Half‑Step into an epic Playing‑in‑the‑Band/El Paso/Wharf Rat/Morning Dew suite and finishing with high‑octane Truckin' and One More Saturday Night.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for soaring solos (Big River, Jack Straw) and impeccable tone; noted as beardless at this show adding to his visual charisma.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for deep, melodic bass lines that weave through Here Comes Sunshine and other jams; described as delivering the goods throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is lauded for rhythmic contributions in the jams, especially during the Playing‑in‑the‑Band/Wharf Rat sequence, adding jazzy texture.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill's drumming is mentioned as solid and supportive, forming a reliable backbone for the extended improvisations.
